troubleshootPage.title: Troubleshoot
troubleshootPage.subTitle: Does the app not work as expected? Here you can find some common solutions to problems.

firewall.symptom: This device can send files to other devices but other devices cannot send files to this device.
firewall.solution: This is most likely a firewall issue. You can solve this by allowing incoming connections (UDP and TCP) on port {port}.

noDiscovery.symptom: This device cannot discover other devices.
noDiscovery.solution: Please make sure that all devices are on the same Wi-Fi network and share the same configuration (port, multicast address, encryption). You can try to type the IP address of the target device manually. If this works, consider adding this device to the favorites so it can be automatically discovered in the future.

noConnection.symptom: Both devices cannot discover each other nor can they share files.
noConnection.solution: Does the problem exist on both sides? If so, you need to make sure that both devices are on the same Wi-Fi network and share the same configuration (port, multicast address, encryption). The Wi-Fi network may not allow communication between participants due to Access Point (AP) Isolation. In this case, this option must be disabled on the router.

aboutPage.title: About Quick Send
description: Quick Send is a free, open-source app for securely sharing files and messages with nearby devices over your local network, without an internet connection.
Quick Send is currently available on Android and Linux.

qsSettings.autostartOfferBody: Quick Send then waits in the system tray after you sign in, so nearby and trusted devices can send you files without opening the app. You can change this in Settings › Desktop.

qsSettings.autoAcceptDesc: Files go straight to your download location
qsSettings.pinDesc: Senders must enter a 4-digit PIN shown here
qsSettings.contextMenuDesc: Adds “Send with Quick Send” to the right-click menu of Files (Nautilus) and Dolphin
qsSettings.privacyText: Nearby sharing works on your local network: files and messages travel directly between devices over an encrypted (HTTPS) connection and are never uploaded to a server. "Over the internet" (only when you use it) connects the two devices directly when possible, otherwise through an iroh relay server (n0, by default) that forwards the end-to-end encrypted data without being able to read it; the relay and the other device can see your IP address. Anyone who has a code can download those files while you are sharing. Update checks contact GitHub (api.github.com) about every 12 hours when automatic updates are on, and when you check manually. Quick Send does not collect analytics or personal data. Your device name and a random device ID are shared only with devices on the same network so that they can find you.
qsSettings.autoFinishDesc: Close the transfer screen when it is done
